subject: How to fit slm model with the error term not follow iid distribution？

messages.author: 551aded02f98012e
messages.subject: How to fit slm model with the error term not follow iid distribution？
parts:
Hi all,

The slm latent model could implement random effect following:

                                                    x=(I_n-rho*W)^(-1)(X*beta+epsilon)
I'm wondering whether there is a way to fit the slm that epsilon has zero mean and precision matrix Q =tau*C(generic0 model).

I think this wouldn't change the slm as a GMRF.So theoretically,I think it is possible.The problem is I can't figure out how to implement it,cause I can't find the 'slm' section's R code to do a little change in 'iid' part.Or I need to read the book GMRF(Rue,2005) then try write all code by myself?

Thank you for any help in advance.

Regards,

Youzi

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to fit slm model with the error term not follow iid distribution？
parts:
I would suggest trying:
1. Fix the likelihood noise to be very small, e.g. logprecision = 8
2. Use generic0 to add your noise as a random effect to the model
3. When reporting the linear predictor, manually sample from the not-noise components and compute what you need

PS: Your product structure may make this impossible, depending on details. My tip is general for "I want correlated noise in my model"

Best,
Haakon
